text:
Tara: Hey team — I just opened my first PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/42. Quick q: what's our branch naming convention and where's the style guide? PR template asks for 'perf impact' — not sure what to put.

Ed: Congrats! Branching: feat/<ticket>-short-desc or fix/<ticket>-short-desc. For experiments use wip/<yourname>/<desc>. Example: `git checkout -b feat/PROJ-123-add-logging`.

Sam: Style guide lives in repo at docs/contributing.md and docs/style/python.md. Also check .eslintrc and pyproject.toml. Highlights: black + isort for python, eslint + prettier for JS, 100-char wrap, type hints on public funcs, and docstrings for exported APIs.

Tara: Nice — do we have pre-commit hooks or a make target to run formatters locally?

Prashant: Yes — run `pre-commit install` then `pre-commit run --all-files`. We also have `make lint` and `make format`. Quick setup: 
```
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
pre-commit install
make format
```
If CI fails on lint, it will show the failing files in the job.

Ed: CI auto-runs black/isort/eslint. If CI fails, paste the failing job link and ping me or @oncall-eng; common fix is running `pre-commit run` locally or applying black.

Tara: Who do I assign as reviewers? I see CODEOWNERS but not sure for infra/runtime dirs.

Sam: CODEOWNERS covers most top-level services. For infra/runtime changes look at docs/oncall/infra-reviews.md. If you're touching runtime, add label `runtime` and tag @infra_team. Generally pick two reviewers: one area owner + one devex/ops reviewer for style/compat.

devex-bot: [bot] Welcome Tara! :tada: Quick checklist: run pre-commit, include a changelog entry if user-visible, add perf numbers under the PR template if latency/cost changes.

Tara: About the PR template perf section — what's expected? A short microbenchmark?

Prashant: If it affects inference/pipelines, run the local perf script under `benchmarks/` and paste median p50/p90 for the changed path. If it's purely docs or tests, say N/A. Example: `python benchmarks/run_perf.py --model small --reps 50`.

Ed: Merge strategy: we generally squash-merge feature branches for a single clean commit. For large refactors that benefit from history, keep commits and request a standard merge. Add `Allow edits from maintainers` if you want help rebasing.

Tara: One CI hiccup — my GPU integration test failed intermittently earlier. Is that a known flake?

Sam: Sometimes the GPU runner times out. If it's flaky, re-run the job from GitHub UI; if it recurs, add `ci: flaky gpu` label and ping @Prashant. We try to mark flakes and track them.

Tara: Cool — I'll re-run pre-commit, add the perf numbers (N/A for this change), fix lint, and push. Thanks for the quick answers! :rocket: 

Ed: Welcome aboard and congrats on the first PR — looking forward to reviewing it :shipit:

Sam: If you want a walkthrough on the repo layout, ping me and I'll do a quick walk-through.

Prashant: FYI — if your change touches model-serving, add a short note in /e2e/evals with the validation prompt set you used.

Tara: Will do. Thanks again!
